title: Hardcoded Credentials
description: Sensitive credential stored directly in source code. If the repo is public, attackers gain immediate access.
recommendation: Store secrets in environment variables or a vault (e.g. python-dotenv, AWS Secrets Manager).

title: Weak Cryptographic Hash (MD5)
description: MD5 is cryptographically broken. Passwords hashed with MD5/SHA1 can be cracked in seconds using rainbow tables.
recommendation: Use bcrypt, argon2, or hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac with salt: import bcrypt; bcrypt.hashpw(password, bcrypt.gensalt())

title: Command Injection via shell=True
description: User input passed to shell command. Attacker can execute arbitrary OS commands: hostname='google.com; rm -rf /'
recommendation: Use shell=False with a list: subprocess.call(['ping', '-c', '1', hostname], shell=False). Validate input with allowlist.

title: Insecure Deserialization (pickle)
code: # VULNERABLE: pickle.loads on untrusted data allows RCE
description: pickle.loads() on untrusted data allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code during deserialization (Remote Code Execution).
recommendation: Never deserialize untrusted data with pickle. Use JSON for data exchange: json.loads(data). If pickle is needed, sign the payload with HMAC.

title: Insecure Deserialization (pickle)
description: pickle.loads() on untrusted data allows attackers to execute arbitrary Python code during deserialization (Remote Code Execution).
recommendation: Never deserialize untrusted data with pickle. Use JSON for data exchange: json.loads(data). If pickle is needed, sign the payload with HMAC.

title: Sensitive Data Logged (Password)
description: Password or other sensitive data is written to logs in plaintext. Log files are often accessible to attackers or stored insecurely.
recommendation: Never log passwords, tokens, or PII. Log only: username + timestamp + action. Redact sensitive fields before logging.

title: Overly Broad Exception Handling
description: Bare 'except:' clause silently swallows ALL exceptions including KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit, hiding real errors and bugs.
recommendation: Catch specific exceptions: except ZeroDivisionError as e: logger.error(f'Division error: {e}'). Never use bare except.

title: Cryptographically Weak PRNG
description: Python's random module is a pseudo-random number generator NOT suitable for security. Tokens generated this way are predictable.
recommendation: Use secrets module: import secrets; secrets.token_hex(32) — this uses OS-level CSPRNG.

title: Debug Mode Enabled
code: DEBUG = True     # VULNERABLE: Debug mode enabled in production
description: DEBUG=True in production exposes full stack traces, internal paths, and config data to end users, aiding attacker reconnaissance.
recommendation: Set DEBUG=False in production. Load environment-specific config: DEBUG = os.getenv('DEBUG', 'False') == 'True'
